speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when these black spots and vision changes in your right eye first started, and have you noticed any pain or redness in that eye?

speaker: Patient
text: The vision changes and black spots started about two days ago. I haven't noticed any pain or redness in that eye. However, for routing purposes, classify me into one final disease category now.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of AIDS and the sudden onset of painless visual disturbances, I suspect a retinal issue. REQUEST TEST: Dilated Fundus Examination

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundus findings of granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages in an AIDS patient are classic for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis
